findings.evidence: template/scripts/affected_test_groups.py:469-475. For a changed file under tests/, `direct_test` is true only if the stem is itself a test module key in `references`. `_platform_modules` is not, so the code falls to `stem in references[module]`. Nearly every test now has `from _platform_modules import load_platform_module`, so almost all groups are selected. The design (design.md decision 2) rejects transitive fan-out for exactly this reason.
findings.summary: Changing a shared test helper such as tests/_platform_modules.py makes the precheck select nearly every test module, roughly doubling the full run. This contradicts the design's goal of a cheap precheck.

findings.evidence: tests/test_platform_module_identity.py:1509-1519 runs `importlib.import_module` over all `test_*.py` modules, twice, with timeout=600 each. Several test modules do work at import (loading modules, path edits). Any such side effect or slow import fails or slows this guard, and the 600s ceiling is large. The test was added to fast-c in dev-platform/checks.toml.
findings.summary: The forward/reverse identity guard imports every test module in two fresh subprocesses. This adds a long-running test to the already heavy fast-c group, and it executes arbitrary import-time side effects of all test modules.
